beats.narration: At 07:52 on Fri 6 Nov 2026, a new email address claims Grace's full $200,000 trauma cover for breast cancer, marked urgent, to be paid into a new account ending 4471 in the name “G Williams Consulting Pty Ltd”.
Olivia's agent extracts a trauma claim, a bank change and a recent contact change: Grace's mobile and email were changed by phone on Mon 2 Nov, about 93 hours before the claim.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261106-LIF002 (CL-100377), sets the priority to Urgent and routes it to Claims.

Ben's agent checks Lyrebird Life policy LB-19004417: a cancer claim needs a confirmed specialist diagnosis with histopathology, and benefits are paid to the policy owner, so a new account in another name can't be used. It refers the case to Felix.

Felix's agent rates the risk HIGH and explains each flag without accusing Grace: the oncologist's report is fake (pasted letterhead, edited dates, no histopathology), the licence photo has been edited, the account opened on 3 Nov is in another name, a new device logged in from Sydney, and Grace's travel notice says she is in Italy until 1 Dec.
Theo approves the block, restores Grace's verified contact details, locks her portal access and approves alerting Lyrebird Life's fraud team: each one a human decision.
Ben confirms that no claim was lodged with Lyrebird Life.
Cara calls Grace on her verified mobile, 0491 570 157. Grace, in Florence, is well and never asked for anything. A reassurance letter follows, with steps to protect her identity.

result.headline: Claim blocked — Grace's cover is safe
result.summary: Outcome: BLOCKED — no claim lodged and $200,000 protected. Grace's $500,000 life cover and $200,000 trauma cover are safe.
